title: Design and synthesis of some benzothiazole hybrids as VEGFR-2-targeting anti-prostate cancer agents and their computational studies
content: Herein, we synthesized some benzothiazole–thiazolidine-2,4-dione–isoxazole hybrids (7a–7n) via Knoevenagel condensation and Cu(i)-catalyzed one-pot regioselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition as key approaches. Later, an MTT assay was used to assess the anti-prostate cancer efficacy of the hybrids (7a–7n) against human cancer cell lines (PC3 and DU-145). Among them, compounds 7f–7i surpassed 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) (IC50 = 37.8 µM) against DU-145, with IC50 values in the range of 21.2–34.2 µM. Additionally, compound 7f showed comparable VEGFR-2 inhibition (IC50 = 32.3 nM) to sorafenib (IC50 = 31.5 nM), while compound 7g showed promising VEGFR-2 inhibition (IC50 = 36.6 nM) compared to sorafenib. Molecular docking against VEGFR-2 (PDB ID: 3VHE) revealed that compounds 7f–7i showed better binding energies and inhibition constants than sorafenib. Interestingly, the binding energies and inhibition constants of 7f and 7g were found to be consistent with the VEGFR-2 inhibition data. Finally, the DFT investigation of 7f revealed a conjugated donor–π–acceptor system with good charge transfer properties. The negative electrostatic potential of carbonyl oxygen suggests possible interactions with VEGFR-2.
